title: Debouncing signals with debounced
description: Learn how to use Angular debounced to delay reacting to signal values until they stop changing.

blocks.text: debounced is experimental. It's ready for you to try, but it might change before it is stable.
Use debounced to delay reacting to a signal's value until it stops changing. It returns a Resource whose value reflects the debounced value of the source signal.

code: import { Component, debounced, resource, signal } from '@angular/core';

blocks.text: debounced takes the source signal and a wait duration in milliseconds. The returned resource's value() always contains the last settled value, and status() tells you whether a new value is still pending.

While the debounce timer is counting down, status() is 'loading' and value() returns the previously resolved value. When the timer expires, the resource settles to 'resolved'. If the source signal throws, the resource enters 'error' immediately; no timer runs.
See Resource status for the full list of statuses and their value() behavior.

Instead of a millisecond duration, you can pass a function that returns a Promise<void>. The resource resolves when the promise resolves. If the source signal changes before the promise settles, Angular discards the previous promise and starts a new one.

blocks.text: See the DebounceTimer type in the API reference for details.
By default, debounced uses Object.is to compare values.
Provide a custom equality function with the equal option when the default identity check is too strict:

code: equal: (a, b) => a.category === b.category && a.minPrice === b.minPrice,

blocks.text: debounced must be called inside an injection context. Angular automatically destroys the debounced resource and cancels any pending timer when the injector is destroyed.
